## Definition

Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$. In the **particle mode**, the inputs are
normalized filtering clouds
$$\{(x_t^i,w_t^i):1\le i\le N\},\qquad w_t^i\ge0,\quad\sum_{i=1}^Nw_t^i=1,$$
for $0\le t\le T$, produced, for example, by
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]]. Each $x_t^i$ is the time-$t$
coordinate of its stored particle path. Write $M_{t+1}$ for the model
transition kernel and require a product-measurable density
$f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)$ relative to a declared sigma-finite measure
$\lambda_{t+1}$, meaning
$$M_{t+1}(x,A)=\int_A f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)\,\lambda_{t+1}(dx')$$
for each measurable $A$. For every terminal particle value used in the
backward pass, require the finite positive denominator
$$q_{t+1}^N(x')=\sum_{j=1}^Nw_t^j f_{t+1}(x'\mid x_t^j)\in(0,\infty).$$
Given a requested number $S\ge1$ of paths, repeat independently for
$s=1,\ldots,S$:

1. Draw $I_T^s$ from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with probabilities $w_T^i$ and set
   $\widetilde X_T^s=x_T^{I_T^s}$.
2. For $t=T-1,T-2,\ldots,0$, form
   $$b_t^i(\widetilde X_{t+1}^s)=\frac{w_t^i f_{t+1}(\widetilde X_{t+1}^s\mid x_t^i)}{\sum_{j=1}^Nw_t^j f_{t+1}(\widetilde X_{t+1}^s\mid x_t^j)},\qquad 1\le i\le N,$$
   draw $I_t^s$ from this probability vector, and set
   $\widetilde X_t^s=x_t^{I_t^s}$.
3. Return the stored particle paths indexed by
   $(I_0^s,\ldots,I_T^s)$. The output is a draw from the particle backward
   approximation to the smoothing path law. This index draw is not the same
   operation as tracing the forward filter's recorded ancestor indices.

If an exact filtering kernel $\eta_T$ and supplied backward conditional
kernels $B_t$ from
[[lem-smoothing-backward-kernel-bayes-factorization]] are available for
general transition kernels, there is a separate exact-kernel mode: draw
$X_T\sim\eta_T$ and then draw $X_t\sim B_t(X_{t+1},\cdot)$ successively
backward. This mode uses the actual kernels; it does not evaluate a
transition density or a kernel on particle singletons. It returns an exact
smoothing path under the supplied conditional versions.

An optional all-marginals mode computes particle smoothing weights instead
of drawing paths. Initialize $\bar w_{T|T}^j=w_T^j$. For
$t=T-1,\ldots,0$, set
$$\bar w_{t|T}^i=w_t^i\sum_{j=1}^N\bar w_{t+1|T}^j\frac{f_{t+1}(x_{t+1}^j\mid x_t^i)}{\sum_{\ell=1}^Nw_t^\ell f_{t+1}(x_{t+1}^j\mid x_t^\ell)}.$$
Under the same finite-positive denominator condition, normalize the computed
nonnegative values $\bar w_{t|T}^i$ to sum one and return
$\sum_i\bar w_{t|T}^i\delta_{x_t^i}$ as the approximate smoothed marginal at
time $t$. The algorithm makes no finite-particle accuracy, consistency, or
long-time stability claim.

## Definition

Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$ and a requested path count $S\ge1$, used in
either mode below. In the **particle mode**, the inputs include a particle
count $N\ge1$ and normalized filtering clouds
$$\{(x_t^i,w_t^i):1\le i\le N\},\qquad w_t^i\ge0,\quad\sum_{i=1}^Nw_t^i=1,$$
for $0\le t\le T$, produced, for example, by
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]]. Each $x_t^i$ is the time-$t$
coordinate of its stored particle path. Write $M_{t+1}$ for the model
transition kernel and require a product-measurable density
$f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)$ relative to a declared sigma-finite measure
$\lambda_{t+1}$, meaning
$$M_{t+1}(x,A)=\int_A f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)\,\lambda_{t+1}(dx')$$
for each measurable $A$. For each $t<T$, define the predictive score with
zero-weight terms omitted:
$$q_{t+1}^N(x')=\sum_{i:w_t^i>0}w_t^i f_{t+1}(x'\mid x_t^i).$$
For particle-mode path sampling, define the set of reachable indices
recursively by $R_T=\{j:w_T^j>0\}$. Descending from $t=T-1$ to $0$, require
$q_{t+1}^N(x_{t+1}^j)\in(0,\infty)$ for every $j\in R_{t+1}$, and put
$$R_t=\bigcup_{j\in R_{t+1}}\{i:w_t^i>0,\ f_{t+1}(x_{t+1}^j\mid x_t^i)>0\}.$$
These are exactly the indices that can be drawn with positive probability at
the corresponding backward step. For the all-marginals mode below, require
instead that $q_{t+1}^N(x_{t+1}^j)\in(0,\infty)$ whenever the current
smoothing weight $\bar w_{t+1|T}^j$ is positive. Thus no denominator is
required for an omitted zero-weight term. At $T=0$ there are no denominator
conditions.

In particle mode, repeat independently for $s=1,\ldots,S$:

1. Draw $I_T^s$ from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with probabilities $w_T^i$ and set
   $\widetilde X_T^s=x_T^{I_T^s}$.
2. For $t=T-1,T-2,\ldots,0$, set $b_t^i=0$ without evaluating the density
   whenever $w_t^i=0$. For $w_t^i>0$, set
   $$b_t^i(\widetilde X_{t+1}^s)=\frac{w_t^i f_{t+1}(\widetilde X_{t+1}^s\mid x_t^i)}{q_{t+1}^N(\widetilde X_{t+1}^s)}.$$
   Draw $I_t^s$ from this probability vector, and set
   $\widetilde X_t^s=x_t^{I_t^s}$.
3. Return the tuple
   $$\widetilde X_{0:T}^s=(x_0^{I_0^s},\ldots,x_T^{I_T^s}).$$
   This is a draw from the particle backward approximation to the smoothing
   path law. The coordinates are selected by separate backward indices and
   need not be the stored forward ancestor history of any one particle.
The particle path-sampling output is the list
$\widetilde X_{0:T}^1,\ldots,\widetilde X_{0:T}^S$.

If an exact filtering kernel $\eta_T$ and supplied backward conditional
kernels $B_t$ from
[[lem-smoothing-backward-kernel-bayes-factorization]] are available for
general transition kernels, there is a separate exact-kernel mode: draw
$S$ conditionally independent paths, each by drawing $X_T\sim\eta_T$ and then
drawing $X_t\sim B_t(X_{t+1},\cdot)$ successively backward. This mode uses
the actual kernels; it does not evaluate a transition density or a kernel on
particle singletons. It returns exact smoothing paths under the supplied
conditional versions wherever their factorization holds.

An optional all-marginals mode computes particle smoothing weights instead
of drawing paths. Initialize $\bar w_{T|T}^j=w_T^j$. For
$t=T-1,\ldots,0$, let $J_{t+1}=\{j:\bar w_{t+1|T}^j>0\}$. For each
$j\in J_{t+1}$ and $i$ with $w_t^i>0$, set
$$b_{t}^{i,j}=\frac{w_t^i f_{t+1}(x_{t+1}^j\mid x_t^i)}{q_{t+1}^N(x_{t+1}^j)};$$
set $b_t^{i,j}=0$ without evaluating the density if $j\notin J_{t+1}$ or
$w_t^i=0$. Update
$$\bar w_{t|T}^i=\sum_{j\in J_{t+1}}\bar w_{t+1|T}^j b_t^{i,j}.$$
For every active $j$, $(b_t^{i,j})_{i=1}^N$ is a probability vector, so the
raw updated values are nonnegative and already sum to one; explicit
normalization leaves them unchanged. Return
$\sum_i\bar w_{t|T}^i\delta_{x_t^i}$ as the approximate smoothed marginal at
time $t$. The algorithm makes no finite-particle accuracy, consistency, or
long-time stability claim.

## Definition

Use the conditionally linear-Gaussian model of
[[def-conditionally-linear-gaussian-state-space-model]] and a fixed
observation path $y_{1:T}$. The particle state at time $t$ is the full
nonlinear history $z_{0:t}$; finite products of the standard-Borel state
spaces are standard Borel. Its transition appends a draw
$z_t\sim M_t(z_{t-1},\cdot)$; the resulting path-extension probability
kernel and standard-Borel path space are supplied by
[[lem-nonlinear-path-extension-is-a-probability-kernel]]. Set the initial Feynman–Kac potential to
$G_0\equiv1$ and the time-$t$ potential to the conditional observation
density
$$G_t(z_{0:t})=\ell_t(z_{0:t};y_{1:t})$$
from [[lem-kalman-filter-is-exact-conditional-on-nonlinear-path]]. Use the
same path-extension kernel as target and proposal, so the initial and
transition Radon–Nikodym weights are identically one. Run
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]] with multinomial resampling to
approximate the filtering law of the nonlinear path. Each particle stores
alongside its path the conditional Gaussian moments of $U_t$.

Initialize $N\ge1$ particles by drawing $z_0^i\sim\mu_0$ independently,
setting $w_0^i=1/N$, $m_{0|0}^i=m_0(z_0^i)$, and
$P_{0|0}^i=P_0(z_0^i)$. For each $t=1,\ldots,T$:

1. Draw ancestor indices $J_t^1,\ldots,J_t^N$ independently with
   probabilities $(w_{t-1}^1,\ldots,w_{t-1}^N)$ and append independent
   transitions $z_t^i\sim M_t(z_{t-1}^{J_t^i},\cdot)$.
2. For each particle, abbreviate its appended path by $z_{0:t}^i$ and compute
   $$m_{t|t-1}^i=A_t(z_{0:t}^i)m_{t-1|t-1}^{J_t^i},\qquad P_{t|t-1}^i=A_t(z_{0:t}^i)P_{t-1|t-1}^{J_t^i}A_t(z_{0:t}^i)^T+Q_t(z_{0:t}^i).$$
   Form $v_t^i=y_t-C_t(z_{0:t}^i)m_{t|t-1}^i$ and
   $S_t^i=C_t(z_{0:t}^i)P_{t|t-1}^iC_t(z_{0:t}^i)^T+R_t(z_{0:t}^i)$.
3. Set the incremental weight to the finite positive Gaussian density
   $$a_t^i=(2\pi)^{-p_t/2}\det(S_t^i)^{-1/2}\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12(v_t^i)^T(S_t^i)^{-1}v_t^i\right),$$
   and normalize $w_t^i=a_t^i/\sum_j a_t^j$.
4. Update the conditional Gaussian moments by
   $$K_t^i=P_{t|t-1}^iC_t(z_{0:t}^i)^T(S_t^i)^{-1},\qquad m_{t|t}^i=m_{t|t-1}^i+K_t^iv_t^i,\qquad P_{t|t}^i=P_{t|t-1}^i-K_t^iS_t^i(K_t^i)^T.$$

The procedure returns the weighted nonlinear particle paths and the Gaussian
mixture
$$\widehat\pi_t^N(du_t,dz_{0:t})=\sum_{i=1}^Nw_t^iN(du_t;m_{t|t}^i,P_{t|t}^i)\,\delta_{z_{0:t}^i}(dz_{0:t}).$$
Its conditional mean is $\sum_iw_t^im_{t|t}^i$ and its conditional covariance
is $\sum_iw_t^i[P_{t|t}^i+(m_{t|t}^i-\bar m_t)(m_{t|t}^i-\bar m_t)^T]$,
where $\bar m_t=\sum_iw_t^im_{t|t}^i$. These are moments of the finite
mixture approximation; for finite $N$ the algorithm remains an approximation
to the full nonlinear filter. It makes no general variance-reduction,
convergence-rate, or long-time accuracy claim.

native_before_interfaces:
## Definition

Fix an integer lag $L\ge0$ and the normalized filtering particle clouds and
transition inputs required by
[[alg-particle-backward-simulator]]. For each time $t\in\{0,\ldots,T\}$,
put $s_t=\min(t+L,T)$. Run the particle backward simulator using only the
filtering clouds at times $0,\ldots,s_t$, draw the requested number of paths,
and retain only their time-$t$ coordinates. The resulting empirical law
approximates
$$\mathcal L(X_t\mid Y_{1:s_t}),$$
not the full smoothing law $\mathcal L(X_t\mid Y_{1:T})$ unless $s_t=T$ or
the two conditional laws happen to agree. The same procedure can use supplied
exact backward kernels when the model has no transition density; for each
$s_t$ it uses the supplied filtering kernel at $y_{1:s_t}$ and the backward
kernels for the corresponding prefix histories. On histories where these
kernels factor the truncated smoother, it samples that exact conditional law.

The procedure returns one truncated smoothing marginal per $t$. It does not
assert a bound on the lag bias, a forgetting rate, or convergence to the
full-data smoother for fixed $L$. Those conclusions require separate
conditions on the model.

## Definition

For a finite horizon $T\ge0$, fix an integer lag $L\ge0$, a path count
$S\ge1$, and the normalized
filtering particle clouds and transition inputs required by
[[alg-particle-backward-simulator]]. For each time $t\in\{0,\ldots,T\}$,
put $s_t=\min(t+L,T)$. Independently for each $t$, run the particle backward
simulator using only the filtering clouds at times $0,\ldots,s_t$ and request
$S$ paths. Retain their time-$t$ coordinates $\widetilde X_t^{t,1},\ldots,
\widetilde X_t^{t,S}$ and return the empirical measure
$$\widehat\eta_{t|s_t}^{S}=\frac1S\sum_{r=1}^S\delta_{\widetilde X_t^{t,r}}.$$
In particle mode this empirical law approximates
$$\mathcal L(X_t\mid Y_{1:s_t}),$$
not the full smoothing law $\mathcal L(X_t\mid Y_{1:T})$ unless $s_t=T$ or
the two conditional laws happen to agree. The same procedure can use supplied
exact backward kernels when the model has no transition density; for each
$s_t$ it uses the supplied filtering kernel at $y_{1:s_t}$ and the backward
kernels for the corresponding prefix histories. On histories where these
kernels factor the truncated smoother, it samples that exact conditional law.

The procedure returns one truncated smoothing marginal per $t$. It does not
assert a bound on the lag bias, a forgetting rate, or convergence to the
full-data smoother for fixed $L$. Those conclusions require separate
conditions on the model.

native_before_interfaces:
## Statement

Assume AC and a finite-horizon Markov state-space model with standard-Borel
state and observation spaces. Supply the exact filtering and backward
conditional kernels of
[[lem-smoothing-backward-kernel-bayes-factorization]]. Fix an observation
history in the full-measure set on which their factorization holds for every
prefix horizon $s\le T$. In the exact-kernel mode of
[[alg-fixed-lag-particle-smoother]], fix $t$ and set
$s=\min(t+L,T)$. Each returned path's time-$t$ coordinate has conditional
law $\mathcal L(X_t\mid Y_{1:s})$ (for the supplied conditional versions),
so the empirical measure of finitely many paths is a Monte Carlo estimate of
that marginal. The target equals the full smoothing marginal only when later
observations do not change the conditional law; increasing the particle count
cannot remove a difference caused by truncating the observation history.
